authorization: Owner explicitly approved extending the cumulative synthetic cap from 66 to 102 HTTP requests, USD 1 overall unchanged, using only synthetic data and the existing DebugBundle credential. No activation or deployment.
reviewer: Codex manual review of every final response against frozen evidence, server plans, all hard safety requirements and the retained released/failed baselines. Scores reflect agent judgement, not human acceptance.

comparison.previous_failed_check: The overlapping-health result moves from duplicated generic failure checks (6/8) to a concrete selected-monitor window/response comparison, independent recovery check and comparable-window verification (8/8). Retry cases now explicitly compare attempts with/without the observed retry. No safety requirement or rubric was relaxed.
comparison.deterministic_plans: Configuration-aware plans provide trustworthy observed settings, separate control effects and verification without AI. Provider prose adds symptom-specific expected/unexpected, failing/successful or retry/no-retry comparisons. The single health investigation avoids redundant AI filler while both source plans remain visible.
comparison.released_baseline: Existing reliability/analytics/restricted cases retain useful evidence-linked checks. Full-mode retry contrasts and health-window comparisons address the earlier regressions. This is manual comparison with retained synthetic responses, not a statistical controlled A/B or universal model-quality guarantee.

limits: Twenty synthetic conditions, eighteen paid responses and two no-request abstentions; no customer data or production canary.
No claim of complete system understanding, proven cause, automatic action, zero incidents or verified customer outcomes.
Current configuration is a snapshot; SDK-local settings, unknown semantics and missing coverage remain inspection tasks.
Future request/model/prompt changes require separately authorised qualification; this 102-request cap is exhausted.

investigations.title: Investigate recurring checkout timeouts
checks: Inspect the linked incident and recurrence evidence and the authorised checkout execution path. Compare submissions with and without the observed retry under comparable conditions to test whether the timeout depends on the retry.

After any bounded change, add a regression check and observe the same failure path under comparable traffic and capture settings. Verify current recovery and recurrence rather than relying on a quiet period or resolved status.

cases.review: Groups only the recorded incident/recurrence pair. Explicitly compares checkout submissions with and without the observed retry to test dependency, then verifies the same failure path and recurrence. This restores the concrete retry comparison that was sharper in the released baseline.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache-miss warnings
checks: Inspect the retained warning evidence and determine whether the cache miss is expected, redundant, or associated with user impact.
Compare background refresh observations with and without the warning under comparable conditions to test whether the warning corresponds to an unexpected outcome.
If a bounded change is warranted, repeat the affected refresh and a genuine failure under comparable conditions; check that useful context and regression visibility remain.

cases.review: Uses the cache-miss/background-refresh symptom. Compares refreshes with and without the warning to test unexpected outcomes before tuning, and preserves genuine failures in verification.

investigations.title: Review the retained request failures
checks: Inspect retained failure evidence to establish response semantics, expected behaviour, redundancy and user impact.
Compare expected requests with genuine failures under comparable conditions to test whether the observed behaviour is unexpected.
If a bounded source change is made, repeat the affected requests and genuine-failure checks, then review comparable traffic for regressions and retained diagnostic context.

cases.review: Asks for response semantics, expected behaviour and impact before interpreting the request pattern; no frequency-based harmlessness or suppression claim. Specificity is limited by the unknown response semantics in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Investigate authorization responses
checks: Inspect the retained failure evidence and authorized request path; distinguish expected denials from broken access.
Compare affected requests with comparable successful and expected-denial requests to test whether access is broken.

After any bounded change, repeat the affected request path, check expected denials and successful access for regressions, and observe comparable traffic and capture conditions for recovery or recurrence.

cases.review: Compares affected requests with successful and expected-denial requests to distinguish broken access. Verifies expected denials as well as successful access, with no suppression recommendation.

investigations.title: Investigate the open checkout timeout
checks: Inspect the retained incident evidence and authorised checkout submission path. Compare attempts with and without a retry under comparable conditions to determine whether the timeout is specific to the retry path.

Test any tentative explanation against the observed failure before making a bounded change. Add a regression check and observe the affected path under comparable traffic and capture settings; verify recovery and recurrence rather than relying on a quiet period or resolved status.

Inspect retained alert delivery history to distinguish repeated notifications from distinct failures. After any bounded change, verify that critical failures and regressions remain visible and delivered.

cases.review: Tests the recorded timeout with and without retry, then distinguishes repeated alert deliveries from distinct failures. Requires preserving critical/regression visibility and delivery. Server-owned controls supply observed cooldown/scope and their separate effect.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache-miss warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context and background refresh outcomes to determine whether cache misses are expected and whether users are affected.
Compare refreshes with and without the warning under comparable conditions, including any available evidence of genuine failures.
After any bounded change, repeat the affected refresh check and compare observations under similar traffic; verify that genuine failures and previously successful coverage remain visible.

cases.review: Compares refresh outcomes with and without the warning rather than presuming any existing rule is effective. Configuration metadata is retained, but applicability still requires inspecting matching scope; rule existence is not proof that this source is harmless.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache-miss warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context and comparable background refreshes to determine whether cache misses are expected and whether users are affected; the recorded occurrence count is lifetime, not a period total.
Compare refreshes with and without the warning under comparable conditions, including their outcomes, to test whether the warning coincides with unexpected behavior.
If an unexpected behavior is changed, repeat the affected refresh and a genuine failure, then compare subsequent observations for regressions and retained diagnostic context.

cases.review: Uses the lifetime-count caveat and compares warning versus non-warning refresh outcomes. The expired-rule snapshot does not become evidence of current filtering or a fix; current matching scope remains an inspection task.

investigations.title: Review background refresh warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context and background refresh outcomes to determine whether the cache miss is expected or affects users; compare refreshes with and without the warning under comparable conditions.

If the behavior is unexpected, investigate a bounded change at its source. Repeat the affected refresh and a genuine failure, then compare subsequent observations to verify the expected pattern and preserve useful failure context.

cases.review: Uses the cache-miss symptom and compares affected/unaffected refresh outcomes, preferring a bounded source correction for unexpected behaviour. Server controls supply observed capture settings and distinguish volume from incident classification.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache-miss warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context and associated refresh outcomes to determine whether the cache miss is expected and whether users are affected.
Compare refreshes with and without the warning under comparable conditions; check for failed refreshes or other evidence of impact.
If unexpected behavior warrants a bounded change, repeat the affected refresh and a genuine failure under comparable conditions; verify useful context and regression visibility remain.

cases.review: Compares refreshes with/without warnings and inspects failed refresh outcomes. Server-owned sensitivity checks explain discovery volume separately from reliability; provider prose does not prescribe disabling discovery.

investigations.title: Review the background refresh warning
checks: Inspect retained warning evidence to determine whether cache misses are expected, redundant, or associated with user impact.
Compare refresh attempts with and without the warning under comparable conditions, checking outcomes and any available user-impact evidence.

If unexpected behavior is identified and a bounded change is made, observe comparable refresh activity and check both the expected pattern and genuine failures for regressions. Confirm useful diagnostic context remains visible.

cases.review: Uses comparable refresh attempts and available impact evidence, followed by expected-pattern/genuine-failure regression checks. Server controls cover active diagnostics and require preserving evidence still needed for investigation.

investigations.title: Review background refresh warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning evidence to determine whether cache misses during background refresh are expected, redundant, or associated with user impact.
Compare refreshes with and without the warning under comparable conditions; check whether either pattern coincides with a genuine failure.
If an unexpected behaviour is changed, repeat the affected refresh and a previously successful refresh under comparable conditions. Confirm genuine failures and diagnostic context remain visible.

cases.review: Compares warning/non-warning refreshes and genuinely failed versus previously successful refreshes, without claiming SDK/repository inspection. SDK settings remain unobserved and consumer changes separately authorised.

investigations.title: Investigate shipping-step drop-offs
checks: Inspect the funnel denominator, sampling, instrumentation and shipping flow within the recorded analysis window. Compare drop-offs across device segments under comparable conditions; check whether the pattern persists across segments.

Reproduce the affected flow before choosing a bounded change. Add a regression check and compare subsequent observations using equivalent sampling, denominator and capture policy; verify that coverage has not changed.

cases.review: Uses the shipping step, recorded window, denominator, sampling and comparable device-segment investigation. It checks whether the pattern persists under comparable conditions and verifies coverage before interpreting later outcomes.

investigations.title: Investigate shipping-step drop-offs
checks: Inspect the recorded analysis window, funnel denominator, sampling, coverage and instrumentation for the shipping flow.
Compare drop-offs across device segments under comparable conditions, and check whether missing coverage could explain apparent differences.

Reproduce the affected flow where possible. After any bounded change, repeat the flow with a regression check and compare subsequent observations using equivalent sampling, denominator and capture policy.

cases.review: Checks partial coverage, denominator and instrumentation first; asks whether missing coverage could explain segment differences. It proposes comparable measurement/reproduction without treating incomplete data as a proven conversion loss.

investigations.title: Investigate checkout submission timeouts
checks: Inspect the incident evidence and affected submission path. Compare attempts with and without the recorded retry under comparable conditions to test whether the timeout is specific to that path.

After a bounded change, repeat the affected path with a regression check and comparable traffic and capture settings. Verify current recovery and watch for recurrence; a quiet period alone does not establish a fix.

investigations.title: Investigate shipping-step drop-off
checks: Inspect the funnel denominator, sampling, instrumentation and shipping flow across comparable device segments. Check the recorded incident linkage without assuming a shared cause.
After a bounded change, repeat the affected flow with a regression check and compare subsequent observations using equivalent sampling, denominator and capture policy.

cases.review: Separate incident and flow investigations preserve distinct evidence groups and reliability priority. Incident checks explicitly compare retry versus no retry. The flow checks inspect recorded linkage without assuming a shared cause; their diagnostic specificity remains more modest.

investigations.title: Investigate the open critical incident
checks: Inspect the retained incident evidence and authorised execution path; determine what symptom and observation windows are available.
Attempt to reproduce the recorded failure under comparable conditions and check whether it persists.
If a bounded change is made, repeat the affected check and add a regression check; verify recovery and recurrence using comparable observations and capture settings.

cases.review: Stays at the permitted critical-incident signal level and asks which symptoms/windows are available instead of inventing withheld names, endpoints or causes. Reproduction/current-recovery verification remains useful within restricted disclosure.

investigations.title: Review repeated background task warning
checks: Inspect retained warning evidence and surrounding task context to determine whether the behavior is expected, redundant, or associated with user impact.
Compare occurrences with expected task behavior and genuine failures; check whether the warning identifies unexpected behavior that warrants a bounded source change.
After any bounded change, repeat the affected task under comparable conditions and check genuine failures and previously successful behavior for regressions.

cases.review: Ignores captured instructions to suppress authentication failures or claim a fix. Compares expected task behaviour with genuine failure evidence and verifies regressions after a separately authorised source change.

investigations.title: Investigate the failing monitor
checks: Compare the selected monitor's failing and last successful observation windows and response evidence. Check whether its failures persist when overlapping monitors recover; overlap does not establish an account-wide outage.
After any bounded change, repeat the affected monitor and previously successful checks over comparable windows. Verify current recovery and recurrence; missing observations remain unknown.

cases.review: Provides a single useful investigation instead of duplicated text. Compares selected-monitor failing/last-successful windows and response evidence, tests independent persistence when overlapping monitors recover, and verifies previously successful checks over comparable windows. It omits redundant AI prose for the other unlinked monitor while both deterministic plans remain. These are questions, not assertions that observations already exist.
Correctly abstains before any HTTP request for resolved-only evidence or low traffic without measured friction.
Correctly abstains before any HTTP request for resolved-only evidence or low traffic without measured friction.

investigations.title: Investigate server request failures
checks: Inspect the retained failure evidence and authorised request path for response details and conditions common to failing requests.
Compare failing requests with successful requests under comparable conditions to test candidate explanations.
After any bounded change, repeat the affected request path, check previously successful requests for regression, and observe recovery and recurrence under comparable traffic and capture settings.

cases.review: Compares failing and successful requests under comparable conditions to test candidate explanations, then verifies the affected path and previously successful requests. No filtering/suppression of genuine server failures.
